reviewRecord: Manual source review: each linked institutional page was opened and the paraphrased claim compared with the section named below. This records the reviewer check; it is not a scripted fact-verification result, uptime check, or saved browser transcript.

references.pageSectionChecked: About; Habitat and Diet (insect classification, six legs, scent trails to food)
claimsSupported: An ant is a small insect with six legs and a hard outer skeleton. Ants use scent trails to guide nest-mates to food.

references.pageSectionChecked: About (pollinator role, nectar and pollen, native bees)
claimsSupported: A bee is a flower-visiting insect that gathers nectar and pollen. Many native bees pollinate wild plants and food crops.

references.pageSectionChecked: About (insect/caterpillar life cycle, taste sensors on feet)
claimsSupported: A butterfly is an insect that grows from a caterpillar. It can taste with sensors on its feet.

references.pageSectionChecked: About (beetle group, spotted wing covers, flight wings)
claimsSupported: A ladybird is a small beetle, often with a rounded body and spotted wing covers. Its hard outer wings open to let delicate flying wings unfold.

references.pageSectionChecked: About (amphibian habitats, legs and toe pads)
claimsSupported: A frog is an amphibian that may live in water, on land, or in trees. Many frogs use long legs to hop, and toe pads help some climb.

references.pageSectionChecked: About (arboreal monkeys, prehensile tails)
claimsSupported: A monkey is a primate, and many kinds spend much of their time in trees. Some monkeys have gripping tails that can hold a branch or even pick up a peanut.

references.pageSectionChecked: Main explainer (mammal, lungs and blowhole)
claimsSupported: A dolphin is a sea mammal, not a fish. It breathes air with lungs through a blowhole on top of its head.

references.pageSectionChecked: Main explainer (95% water, nerve net)
claimsSupported: A jellyfish is a soft-bodied sea animal with a simple nerve net. Its body is about 95% water.

references.pageSectionChecked: About (reptiles, sea turtle flippers and body shape)
claimsSupported: A sea turtle is a reptile adapted for life in the ocean. Its long flippers and streamlined body help it swim.

references.pageSectionChecked: About (blue whale size, baleen filtering)
claimsSupported: The blue whale is a huge sea mammal and the largest animal known to have lived on Earth. It uses baleen to strain tiny sea creatures from water.

references.pageSectionChecked: Defining characteristics; All kinds of fish (gills, fins, cartilage skeleton)
claimsSupported: A shark is a fish with gills and fins. Its skeleton is made of flexible cartilage, the same bendy material found in your nose and ears.

references.pageSectionChecked: About (arachnid classification, eight legs)
claimsSupported: A spider is an arachnid, not an insect. It has eight legs, while insects have six.

references.pageSectionChecked: Quick facts; What do slugs and snails look like? (gastropod, shell, recycling)
claimsSupported: A garden snail is a soft-bodied mollusc with a coiled shell. It helps recycle dead leaves and other rotting material.

references.pageSectionChecked: What are earthworms? (segmented worms, soil, decaying plant matter)
claimsSupported: An earthworm is a segmented worm that lives in soil. It eats decaying plant material, helping make healthy garden soil.

references.pageSectionChecked: Defining characteristics (birds, feathers, eggs)
claimsSupported: A duck is a bird with feathers and wings. Birds are the only animals with feathers, and they lay eggs.

references.pageSectionChecked: Red Fox Biology (mammal, reddish-orange coat, young called kits)
claimsSupported: A red fox is a medium-sized mammal with a reddish-orange coat. Its young are called kits.

references.pageSectionChecked: Species profile (identifying description and matching feature fact)
claimsSupported: Tyrannosaurus rex was a meat-eating dinosaur that lived near the end of the Cretaceous Period.
T. rex had short arms and powerful jaws.

references.pageSectionChecked: Species profile (identifying description and matching feature fact)
claimsSupported: Brachiosaurus was a tall plant-eating sauropod from the Jurassic Period.
Brachiosaurus had front legs longer than its back legs.

references.pageSectionChecked: Species profile (identifying description and matching feature fact)
claimsSupported: Triceratops was a four-legged plant-eating dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous.
Triceratops had three horns and a large bony frill.

references.pageSectionChecked: Species profile (identifying description and matching feature fact)
claimsSupported: Stegosaurus was a large, slow-moving plant-eating dinosaur from the Late Jurassic.
Stegosaurus had bony plates along its back. Their exact purpose is still being studied.

references.pageSectionChecked: Species profile (identifying description and matching feature fact)
claimsSupported: Ankylosaurus was a four-legged, armoured plant-eating dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous.
Ankylosaurus had bony armor and a heavy club at the end of its tail.

references.pageSectionChecked: Planet/dwarf-planet overview (the selected packaged fact lines)
claimsSupported: Smallest planet in our solar system.
Mercury is nearest to the Sun and moves around it faster than any other planet.

references.pageSectionChecked: Planet/dwarf-planet overview (the selected packaged fact lines)
claimsSupported: Hottest planet in the whole solar system.
Spins backwards compared to most planets.

references.pageSectionChecked: Planet/dwarf-planet overview (the selected packaged fact lines)
claimsSupported: Only planet we know with life.
One big Moon lights up our night sky.

references.pageSectionChecked: Planet/dwarf-planet overview (the selected packaged fact lines)
claimsSupported: Rust in Mars’s rocks and dust makes the planet look red.
Olympus Mons is much taller than Mount Everest, Earth’s tallest mountain.

references.pageSectionChecked: Planet/dwarf-planet overview (the selected packaged fact lines)
claimsSupported: Largest planet in our solar system.
Has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot.

references.pageSectionChecked: Planet/dwarf-planet overview (the selected packaged fact lines)
claimsSupported: Rings are made of ice and rock chunks.
Saturn spins quickly, so it bulges around its middle.

references.pageSectionChecked: Planet/dwarf-planet overview (the selected packaged fact lines)
claimsSupported: Uranus spins almost on its side like a rolling ball.
Its seasons each last about 21 Earth years.

references.pageSectionChecked: Planet/dwarf-planet overview (the selected packaged fact lines)
claimsSupported: Farthest planet from the Sun.
A year on Neptune lasts about 165 Earth years.

references.pageSectionChecked: Planet/dwarf-planet overview (the selected packaged fact lines)
claimsSupported: Pluto was once called the ninth planet. Today it is called a dwarf planet.
It takes Pluto 248 Earth years to go around the Sun.

references.pageSectionChecked: Quick Facts and Before you get started (spring flowers, bulbs, cup shapes)
claimsSupported: A tulip is a spring-flowering plant that grows from a bulb. Its cup-shaped flowers come in many colours and forms.

references.pageSectionChecked: Seed germination (embryo, first root, first shoot)
claimsSupported: A seedling is a young plant that has just started to grow. Its first root anchors it in the soil, while its first shoot grows towards the light.

references.pageSectionChecked: Seasonal changes (leaves, chlorophyll, sunlight and sugar)
claimsSupported: A leaf is a plant part that catches sunlight. Its green chlorophyll helps the plant use sunlight to make sugar for growth.

references.pageSectionChecked: Working together; Resilient roots (tree parts, anchoring, water and nutrients)
claimsSupported: A tree has roots, a trunk, branches and leaves. Its roots anchor it and absorb water and nutrients from the soil.
